properties.notes: Dutch man, 70, first to die on board. Symptoms began Apr 6. Body removed at Saint Helena Apr 24. Index case — likely contracted virus during Patagonia shore excursion before departure.
Dutch woman, 69, wife of index case. Disembarked at Saint Helena Apr 24, flew to Johannesburg. Removed from KLM flight KL592 before takeoff, died in hospital Apr 25.
Third confirmed death occurred on board. Cluster of 6 confirmed + 2 probable Andes virus cases. WHO notified 2 May. WHO DON 2026-DON600.
Swiss male, one of 30 passengers who disembarked at Saint Helena Apr 24. Confirmed positive, admitted to Zurich University Hospital. Source: bag.admin.ch
British national, 56, ex-police officer Martin Anstee. Evacuated from ship May 6, treated at Leiden University Medical Center. Confirmed hantavirus.
Dutch national, 41, ship's doctor. Evacuated May 6, plane diverted to Gran Canaria due to life support failure, arrived Netherlands May 7. Tested positive at Radboud University Medical Center.
German national, 65, evacuated from ship May 6. Transferred to University Hospital of Düsseldorf. Confirmed hantavirus. Later tested negative for ongoing infection.
British national, removed from ship at Ascension Island, flown to South Africa for hospital care. Confirmed positive by National Institute for Communicable Diseases of South Africa, May 7.

Island resident, suspected to have contracted virus when ship docked Apr 13–15. Hospitalized on island. British Army paratroopers from 16 Air Assault Brigade parachuted in May 10 with 3,300 kg medical supplies.
Spanish passenger, age 32, on KLM flight KL592 from Johannesburg. Sat two rows behind deceased Dutch woman. Symptomatic, hospitalized in Alicante. Classified lower risk. Onset May 7.
KLM flight attendant on KL592 (Johannesburg–Amsterdam Apr 26). Had close contact with deceased Dutch woman. Admitted to Amsterdam University Medical Center May 7. Tested negative May 8.

Male, 67, Singapore resident. Was on MV Hondius and on same flight from Saint Helena to Johannesburg as deceased Dutch woman. Symptomatic (runny nose), awaiting test results. Source: channelnewsasia.com

17 American passengers repatriated on US government charter flight to Offutt Air Force Base, then transferred to National Quarantine Unit at University of Nebraska Medical Center for monitoring and evaluation. CDC Level 3 emergency response.
3 Canadians isolating: 2 disembarked at Saint Helena Apr 24, 1 flew on same flight as deceased Dutch woman from Saint Helena to Johannesburg.
~30–40 passengers disembarked at Saint Helena Apr 24, from 12 countries. All contact-traced by UK Health Security Agency. Two Britons isolating without symptoms.
All passengers on KLM flight KL592 (Johannesburg–Amsterdam Apr 26) being monitored by GGD Kennemerland. 5 high-risk contacts (assisted deceased woman leaving plane), ~50 lower-risk (within 2 rows).
5 French nationals evacuated from MV Hondius to Paris May 10. Hospitalized 72 hours then 45 days home quarantine. One showed symptoms fitting the virus during the evacuation flight.
2 Georgia residents being monitored by Georgia Department of Public Health after being on MV Hondius.
Multiple UK nationals monitored: 1 left ship at Tristan da Cunha (suspected case), 7 left at Saint Helena (2 isolating), others on KLM flight. UKHSA coordinating.
Confirmed Hantavirus, British National. MV Hondus. ♂ Source: https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON599

Departed ship, Swiss national, confirmed case. MV Hondus. ♂ Source: https://www.bag.admin.ch/en/newnsb/p--A7yPSfxdBqR0N9kZMC

Has runny nose, awaiting test results. Was onbord MV Hondius, raveled on same flight from St Helena to Johannesbug on April 25.. Disembarked April 24th. Age 67, ♂ Source: https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/hantavirus-mv-hondius-ncid-test-virus-isolated-cda-6106671

⚠ Andes virus (South American source — person-to-person transmission possible). MV Hondius voyage departure 1 Apr 2026. Andes virus exposure likely during shore excursion in Patagonia. First symptom onset 6 Apr. WHO DON 2026-DON600.
First ANDV death: Dutch passenger medically evacuated and died. Wife disembarked and later died in Johannesburg. WHO DON 2026-DON600.
South Africa NICD lab-confirmed 2 cases, including 1 death (wife of first victim). British passenger also hospitalised here in critical condition. WHO DON 2026-DON600.
Cluster of 6 confirmed + 2 suspected Andes virus cases on board. Third death occurred on board. WHO notified 2 May 2026. WHO DON 2026-DON599.
MV Hondius docked at Praia 3 days; no passengers disembarked. Contact tracing for local port workers. WHO DON 2026-DON600.
MV Hondius arrived Granadilla de Abona, Tenerife 10 May 2026. All passengers disembarked for repatriation flights to 23 countries. Spanish authorities managing screening. WHO DON 2026-DON600.
3 lab-confirmed Andes virus cases: 1 confirmed death on board (2 May, ship flag state) + 2 confirmed survivors medically evacuated. WHO DON 2026-DON600.
1 lab-confirmed Andes virus case post-disembarkation. WHO DON 2026-DON600.
German nationals repatriated from MV Hondius under monitoring. WHO DON 2026-DON600.

ECDC notified 2 May 2026 via EU EWRS. Cluster of 6 confirmed + 2 probable Andes hantavirus cases on Dutch-flagged cruise ship. 23 nationalities on board including 9 EU/EEA countries. ECDC rapid risk assessment, 10 May 2026.
Dutch passengers among confirmed fatalities. Netherlands notified ECDC via EU EWRS on 2 May 2026. ECDC rapid risk assessment.
German national confirmed fatality linked to MV Hondius cluster. ECDC rapid risk assessment, 10 May 2026.
MV Hondius arrived Grandilla de Abona, Tenerife. Passengers disembarking onto repatriation flights to 6 European countries and Canada. ECDC rapid risk assessment, 10 May 2026.
Hospitalised case repatriated to Switzerland. ECDC rapid risk assessment, 10 May 2026.
30 passengers disembarked at Saint Helena; all contact-traced by UK Health Security Agency. ECDC rapid risk assessment, 10 May 2026.
British passenger hospitalised in critical but stable condition. Second fatality (Dutch woman) also died here. ECDC rapid risk assessment, 10 May 2026.

CDC sent team to Canary Islands 7 May 2026. MV Hondius arrived Tenerife 10 May. 17 Americans repatriated to Nebraska facility. CDC classified as Level 3 emergency response. CDC HAN-00528.
17 American passengers repatriated to Nebraska facility with specialised medical capabilities for monitoring. CDC HAN-00528.
